title: Let the founder revoke an enrolled compute node and enroll it again later, keep a node's key apart from every key that speaks for the founder, a device or this body, and void nodes on restore
problem: Directive section 49 says every physical node gets its own identity, bounded capability, explicit enrollment, scoped authority and revocation. Before this unit a node was only a node.enrolled ledger row. Measured by the unit's test file on the base 66f9d5ac (29 failed, 2 passed): NODE_REVOKE was an unknown command kind; a second NODE_ENROLL for the same node_id was refused by a fact-identity EventError, so a node_id could never be enrolled again; the founder's key, a device key and this body's own identity key were accepted as node keys; a 129-character node_id was accepted; a device delegation record naming NODE_ENROLL verified for it; `greg node` did not exist. Review of the first version found two more: a body restored from a backup listed a node revoked after that backup as ACTIVE, and a founder-signed light cone with budget_usd 10**400 raised OverflowError past every ingest path, so the running body stopped on every restart.
founder_intent_refs: INTENT-20261028-OPUS-MAXIMUS-REISSUE (directive section 49 MULTIPLE BODIES: 'Every physical node gets: its own identity; bounded capability; explicit enrollment; scoped authority; revocation.'; also sections 3 ONE GREG, 4 ALFONSO REMAINS ROOT AUTHORITY, 48 and 58 INFRASTRUCTURE SCALING CLOSURE ('Measured compute bottleneck -> alternatives -> economics -> founder authorization -> enrollment -> workload -> measured improvement'), 71 and 72, the sections the WU-06 unit spec serves; recorded on #227)
INTENT-20261030-BUILD-BEFORE-DEVICE-RUN (build the whole directive first; the founder-device run comes after, as its acceptance; recorded on #227)

INTENT-20261019-UPWARD-ASCENT (existing device-delegation, fact-identity, light-cone and fail-closed restore mechanisms are reused for nodes; this is integration of existing mechanisms, not an invention claim)
baseline: PR base e78e5ef0 (#238's head). The unit was built on 66f9d5ac; e78e5ef0 adds only #238's deliberation JSON and a 4-line host-test change, and was merged into the unit as 927f0704 with no conflicts. At the base: greg/founder.py lists NODE_ENROLL but no NODE_REVOKE, and FounderVerifier accepts a device for any kind its delegation record lists; greg/compute.py enroll_node checks the key's length, parses the light cone and records one node.enrolled fact keyed by node_id; nothing in greg/ reads node.enrolled; there is no node CLI; greg/recovery.py restore_body voids device delegations and approvals but not nodes; LightCone.from_dict calls float() on budget_usd without catching OverflowError.

alternatives.name: Proposed: founder-only NODE_REVOKE, revocable and expiring enrollments with key separation, restore voiding and a node CLI
alternatives.description: NODE_REVOKE is a founder-key command kind, and the verifier refuses a device any kind outside DEVICE_KINDS whatever its delegation record lists. enroll_node refuses an active node_id, a node_id outside 1..128 characters or equal to this body's id, any key ever enrolled for the founder or delegated to a device, this body's own identity key and another active node's key; it accepts an optional expires_at and records each enrollment as its own fact [node_id, command_digest]. revoke_node, node_states, active_nodes, unrevoked_nodes and void_for_restore are new in greg/compute.py; greg/body.py gains one 2-line dispatch branch; restore_body voids every unrevoked enrollment; LightCone.from_dict turns an out-of-range budget into ScopeError; `greg node enroll|revoke|list`.
advantages: Section 49's revocation exists: one founder-signed command ends a node's enrollment, and the same node_id can be enrolled again afterwards
A node key can never be a key that has spoken for the founder (rotated-out keys included), a device (revoked delegations included) or this body
A restore cannot bring back a node the founder revoked after the backup
One founder-signed command with an out-of-range budget no longer stops the body, for every light cone (mission, appraisal, Goal Gravity, node)
Reuses existing mechanisms only; greg/body.py changes by 2 lines
disadvantages: Admission only: nothing yet leases work to a node or verifies anything a node signs, so no capacity is added
enroll_node judges expires_at by this host's clock, because the NODE_ENROLL dispatch line passes no clock and greg/body.py is held for #221
Key separation is one-way: DEVICE_ENROLL and ROTATE_FOUNDER_KEY do not yet refuse an active node's key
After a restore the founder must enroll each still-trusted node again
alternatives.revival_evidence: Retained as proposed; revisit when part a2 (node receipts) is designed or #221 merges.

alternatives.name: Simplest viable: NODE_REVOKE alone
alternatives.description: Add NODE_REVOKE to COMMAND_KINDS and record node.revoked; leave enrollment, the fact identity, restore and the CLI unchanged.
advantages: Smallest diff; closes the literal 'revocation' word of section 49
disadvantages: A revoked node_id still could never be enrolled again, because the fact identity is keyed by node_id alone
The founder's key, a device key or this body's key could still be enrolled as a node key
A restore would bring back a revoked node
No way for the founder to issue or read it without hand-writing an envelope
alternatives.revival_evidence: None expected; the measured base defects each defeat revocation in a real sequence (revoke then re-enrol; restore after revoke).

alternatives.name: Strongest competing design: the whole WU-06 unit now (a and b)
alternatives.description: `greg node serve` with its own key and inbox, a `node.run` capability that leases in-cone actions, Ed25519 node receipts verified against the enrolled key, consumed nonces, lease expiry and revocation, a two-process test on this host, and the N8 predicate infrastructure_scaling_closed in greg/path.py.
advantages: Would make a node do work and give N8 a predicate
Exercises revocation against a real consumer (receipts)
disadvantages: Two processes on one 4-core host add no capacity, so a 'compute.improvement VERIFIED with the leased workload' would be parallelism on the same hardware, not infrastructure scaling (both unit-spec critiques)
Consequence laundering: node.run's manifest class would be judged, not the leased inner action's, unless each inner action is admitted as itself
A third inbox beside greg/remote.py, which #221 edits
Depends on WU-10, WU-09 and MU-C (method gate, earned autonomy, credential handles)
alternatives.revival_evidence: Part a2 as an EXPERIMENT after #221 merges (reuse its inbox), with WU-10, WU-09 and MU-C in place; part b with a predicate that requires a different machine identity and reports 'same_host: no capacity added' otherwise.

alternatives.name: Staged or reversible experiment: part a2 leasing restricted to read_only and internal_write
alternatives.description: Lease only read_only and internal_write inner actions, each admitted by AuthorityOffice and the Gate as itself with node.run's class equal to the inner class; check node receipts against active_nodes (a restore's revocations included).
advantages: Bounded consequence class; tests revocation against a real consumer
disadvantages: Still adds no capacity on one host
Needs this unit's revocation and two-way key separation first
alternatives.revival_evidence: This unit landed, #221 merged, and two-way key separation in place.

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: A node enrolled once is admitted for good: a compromised node key cannot be revoked, its node_id can never be enrolled again, the founder's own key or the body's key can be enrolled as a machine identity, and any later receipt check (part a2) would rest on enrollments that no command can end. Section 49's revocation stays unmet.
advantages: No change to greg/founder.py, greg/compute.py, greg/recovery.py or greg/lightcone.py
Nothing to review while nothing consumes node enrollments
disadvantages: Section 49 revocation unmet, and part a2 would have nothing to check receipts against
A founder-signed cone with an out-of-range budget keeps crash-looping the body (pre-existing, made reachable by any new node CLI)

roles.position: Section 49 names revocation as something every physical node gets, and it was missing. This closes it for admission with the founder key as the only signer, and it keeps the destination: the lease fabric, node-signed receipts and the N8 predicate stay open as parts a2 and b, not dropped.
material_concerns: Must not be presented as infrastructure scaling (section 58) or as N8: no node does work and no capacity is added
VEPMC is 0 and unchanged; the founder-device run is the later acceptance under INTENT-20261030-BUILD-BEFORE-DEVICE-RUN
All keys used are test keys; no second machine was involved

roles.position: Existing mechanisms only: FounderVerifier and the DEVICE_REVOKE pattern, journal fact identities, LightCone, and restore_body's fail-closed voiding. No new store, inbox, scheduler or authority path. greg/body.py gains one 2-line dispatch branch beside NODE_ENROLL. node_states is the one read-only fold that enrollment, revocation, restore and `greg node list` all read.
material_concerns: enroll_node uses this host's clock because the NODE_ENROLL dispatch passes none; revoke_node and the restore get the body's clock
This body's own key is recognised through body_id, a 64-bit digest of the key read from founder.enrolled and body.booted, not the raw key, because enroll_node is not handed the body config
greg/recovery.py's import lines conflict textually with #211 (bounded body memory): both sides edit adjacent import lines; the resolution keeps both

roles.position: Two adversarial reviews of the round-1 head e19c172c were done by separate agents of this same session, one attack and one fidelity. They are not independent sessions and not humans. The attack review confirmed F1 (restore resurrects a revoked node), F2 (body's own key accepted), F3 (cone overflow crashes the body), F4 (one-way key separation) and F5 (host clock); the fidelity review confirmed FID-1 (README said 'crashed'), FID-2 (node_id upper bound untested), FID-3 (`node list` read-only untested) and FID-4 (expiry boundary untested). Round 2 reproduced and fixed F1, F2, F3, FID-1, FID-2 and FID-3. F4 and F5 stay as disclosed limitations; FID-4 was not addressed. The attack review refuted replaying an old NODE_ENROLL after a revoke and re-applying a stale envelope after a crash window: both leave the node REVOKED.
material_concerns: Key separation is one-way: after NODE_ENROLL with key K, a founder-signed DEVICE_ENROLL with K is accepted and the node stays ACTIVE (F4)
With the body clock a day behind the host, an enrollment valid by the body clock is refused (F5)
FID-4: changing the EXPIRED boundary from >= to > survives every test
Nothing consumes active_nodes yet, so revocation is correct state, not yet a stopped node

roles.position: The founder operates nodes with `greg node enroll`, `greg node revoke` (signed like `greg device revoke`) and `greg node list`, which reads through observe() and works while a body holds the writer lock. A refused enrollment goes to rejected/ and the body keeps running. Reversible by reverting the branch; revocations already written stay on the append-only ledger.
material_concerns: After a restore every node is voided and must be enrolled again; the restore report says so under needs_from_founder
A node whose light-cone horizon has passed still lists as ACTIVE unless its expires_at passed; LightCone.admits refuses its actions
The mutant gate is not wired into canonical-ci.yml; the #196 integrator must add it
The full suite was not run locally; Canonical CI on this head has not reported

roles.position: Nothing is deleted or rewritten: revocations and restore voids are appended records, and the round-1 wording error ('crashed') is corrected and recorded, not erased. No personal data is involved. Claims stay at INTEGRATION-TESTED plus two LOCAL-REAL CLI sessions with test keys. Whether a restore should void every node, and whether an elapsed cone horizon should list a node as EXPIRED, are the founder's choices.
material_concerns: Restore voiding adds founder work after every restore (one NODE_ENROLL per trusted node)
`greg node list` can show ACTIVE for a node whose cone no longer admits any action, which may mislead the founder
The CLI session outputs live in the session scratchpad and are not committed; the README rows record them

pass_1.intended_outcome: The founder can end a node's enrollment with one founder-signed command and enroll the same node_id again later; while enrolled, a node's key is never a key that has spoken for the founder, a device or this body; a restored body never revives a node revoked after its backup; and `greg node list` reports each node as ACTIVE, REVOKED or EXPIRED without writing.

advantages.statement: Revocation exists, founder key only, and a node_id can be enrolled again after it
advantages.amplified_value: Part a2 can check every node receipt against active_nodes, so one signed command stops a compromised node; section 49's lifecycle (enroll, revoke, re-enroll, expire) is complete at the admission layer

advantages.statement: A node key can never be a founder, device or body identity key, nor another active node's key
advantages.amplified_value: A node can never become a second founder or impersonate this body; part a2's receipts can never be confused with founder commands. Reverses into a liability only while the reverse direction stays unchecked (D2)

advantages.statement: A restore voids nodes exactly as it voids devices
advantages.amplified_value: One fail-closed recovery story for every delegated identity; a revocation the original applied after the backup cannot be lost

advantages.statement: An out-of-range light-cone budget is a refusal for every cone
advantages.amplified_value: Fixes the class, not the instance: mission, appraisal, Goal Gravity and node cones share LightCone.from_dict, so no founder-signed command can crash-loop the body this way

advantages.statement: Each enrollment is its own fact and the same signed command replays to its retained record
advantages.amplified_value: Crash replay after power loss changes nothing (checked end to end through Body.apply by the fidelity review); an enrollment written by the base code still reads as ACTIVE and can be revoked and re-enrolled

disadvantages.statement: enroll_node judges expires_at, and stamps 'at', by this host's clock
disadvantages.redesigned_response: revoke_node and the restore get the body's clock; the enrollment limit is stated in code and README; the one-line fix (now=now on the NODE_ENROLL dispatch) is handed to the greg/body.py owner after #221

disadvantages.statement: Key separation is one-way: DEVICE_ENROLL and ROTATE_FOUNDER_KEY do not refuse an active node's key
disadvantages.redesigned_response: enroll_node refuses every key that ever spoke for the founder (rotated-out keys too) or a device (revoked too) and this body's key; the reverse needs greg/body.py branches #221 touches; today only a founder-signed command can create the overlap

disadvantages.statement: This body's own key is recognised by its 64-bit body_id digest, not the raw key
disadvantages.redesigned_response: A digest collision gives a false refusal, never an acceptance; the test reads the real key from body.json, so a change to how init_body derives body_id fails it

disadvantages.statement: After a restore the founder must enroll every still-trusted node again
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Listed in the restore report's needs_from_founder, the same burden devices already carry

disadvantages.statement: Admission, not activation: no node does work, no capacity is added, N8 stays unmet
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Parts a2 and b are named with the unit-spec critiques' conditions: inner actions admitted as themselves, read_only/internal_write only at first, and a predicate that requires a different machine identity

disadvantages.statement: An elapsed light-cone horizon does not make a node EXPIRED in node_states
disadvantages.redesigned_response: LightCone.admits refuses every action past the horizon; the display gap is stated and left to a founder decision

disadvantages.statement: greg/recovery.py's import lines conflict textually with #211
disadvantages.redesigned_response: The conflict is two adjacent import lines; keep both. The unit's other recovery.py hunks are separate lines, and the merge into #196's head (which holds #234's drill()) is clean

entries.position: Do not build part a2 (node-signed receipts) until DEVICE_ENROLL and ROTATE_FOUNDER_KEY refuse an active node's key and enroll_node uses the body's clock.
entries.rationale: Once a receipt check trusts active_nodes, a key shared between a node and a device or the founder would let one key speak in two roles.
entries.evidence_threshold: Tests showing DEVICE_ENROLL and ROTATE_FOUNDER_KEY refused with an active node's key, and enrollment judged by a test clock

entries.position: `greg node list` should not show ACTIVE for a node whose light-cone horizon has passed, or should say that its cone admits nothing.

authority_impact.approver: Alfonso Lopez (adoption, any merge, restore voiding of nodes, the horizon display); #196 integrator for intake

migration_plan: None required. An enrollment written by the base code (fact key node_id, no expires_at) reads as ACTIVE under the new fold, and can be revoked and then enrolled again without a fact collision (checked by the fidelity review). New records are additive; the old code ignores node.revoked.

steps: Revert this branch's commits on the child branch, or decline intake into #196 through #238
Revocations and restore voids already written stay on the append-only ledger; the reverted code ignores them, so a revoked node reads as enrolled again until a re-applied change

kill_criteria: A device key, or a node's own key, can sign NODE_ENROLL or NODE_REVOKE
A key enrolled for the founder, delegated to a device, or held by this body is accepted as a node key
A restored body lists as ACTIVE a node that was not enrolled after the restore
A refused node command stops the running body
Part a2 checks a receipt against anything other than active_nodes, or accepts one from a revoked or restore-voided node
